au milieu d’un chemin, et que les passans font bientot périr en le heurtant de toutes parts et le pliant
dans tous les sens’ (Oeuvres complètes iv 245; ‘would be like a shrub that chance had caused to be born in

bending it in every direction’ trans. Bloom). Byron writes of Rousseau in Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage III
lxxviii ll. 1–2 that ‘His love was passion’s essence — as a tree / On fire by lightning’.
